findings.text: the read loop admits a line with no trailing newline as a whole record — when the producer's completing write lands after the loop's first readline, the fragment is parsed through the legacy fallback (reckon/crew/runs.py:1157) and _tick records stream.tell() past it (:3022-3026), so the completion arrives as a second fragment and the record is delivered truncated and in two pieces rather than once whole; the snap narrows this window to the interval between the capture and the loop's first read, and the node's test cannot see it because it completes the record inside the replay read (tests/test_follow_rearm_continues.py:601), before the loop opens.

the arm log opens on pytest's own output and names no revision, tree or command, and the tree its baseline_suite entry names (gates/base-tree) no longer exists, so the base arm's identity rests on the manifest's JSON alone; the 330-to-332 passed delta is exactly the new test's two parametrizations and the five failure ids match across the arms, which is consistent with base-versus-head but not independent of the manifest's own claim, and the control log's traceback cites tests/test_follow_rearm_continues.py:613 where the committed test's assertion sits at :616, so its scratch tree held a different revision of the test than b1ebba90.

the done-when clause comparing the known-flaky noise-pair case over five repeated runs was not executed and not reported as a deviation — the case's id appears in neither arm log and nowhere in the run's own stream, and no log records repeated runs of any case — so where the clause exists to keep a flake in one arm from reading as a regression, the record shows one pass per arm and never says the comparison was skipped.

the boundary probe reads the entire stream into memory to find its last newline (data = stream.read(size), rfind at :2424) where the previous form took one stat, so every attach pays a full-file read and a same-size buffer for one byte of information — streams on this workstation reach 36.9 MB (the 2026-09-17 topology run's stream.jsonl) — and reckon/crew/runs.py:1164 read_stream_events shows the streaming idiom the module uses elsewhere.
